title: Spectral bounds and their limits in Pauli contextuality: exact configurations and a proof of Jonah's Conjecture E

author.name: Alexander S. Donahue
author.orcid_provenance: Supplied by the author; matching public record and authenticated ORCID editor observed, displaying Alexander Donahue and identifier 0009-0006-8168-9648. No independent legal-identity certification.

destinations: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical
abstract:
Spectral methods give rigorous bounds on Pauli contextuality, yet a spectrum need not retain the
information needed by a related completion problem.
For $N$ qubits, $D=2^N$, and any set $S$ of nonidentity Pauli observables, Lean 4 proves Jonah's spectral
floor---satisfied minus violated commuting triples is at most $(D-2)|S|^{3/2}/(6\sqrt{D-1})$---together
with its quaternionic (Kramers) refinement for elliptic quadrics and the five-way saturation equivalence
linking equality to pure states with a single nonzero Pauli modulus. Saturating supports outside the
classical families have exact contextuality degrees 75 (135 four-qubit observables), 480 (496 five-qubit
observables) and 729344 (8128 seven-qubit observables), all proved in Lean with kernel-checked counts. We
relate saturation to two-character sets and flat phase states, and classify a third-level phase-state
family through five qubits.

We then test Jonah's strict law: does a sign carrier's spectrum on a hyperplane section determine its
completion spectrum on the remaining observables? On a 71-point section of the real four-qubit quadric,
two assignments give cospectral $16\times16$ carriers whose $64\times64$ completions have cubic traces
14976 and 15360 and distinct binary minima ($\le344\lt347$). A graph construction extends the gap to every
$N\ge4$ in case C3 (difference $`\tfrac32\,8^{N-1}`$), and variants over $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb C$ and
$\mathbb H$, a cone pair swap and a universal cubic-trace identity yield cospectral carriers with distinct
completion spectra in all nine vertex cases for every $N\ge4$, proving Jonah's Conjecture E. All nine
cases, Corollaries 16 and 18, Lemmas 20 and 21 and the cubic-trace identity are proved in Lean 4 using
standard axioms only, with exact verifiers and Tsotchke demonstrations. The work is AI-assisted and is
neither externally peer reviewed nor a quantum-hardware experiment.

abstract_plain_text:
Spectral methods give rigorous bounds on Pauli contextuality, yet a spectrum need not retain the information needed by a related completion problem. For N qubits, D=2^N, and any set S of nonidentity Pauli observables, Lean 4 proves Jonah's spectral floor -- satisfied minus violated commuting triples is at most (D-2)|S|^(3/2)/(6 sqrt(D-1)) -- together with its quaternionic (Kramers) refinement for elliptic quadrics and the five-way saturation equivalence linking equality to pure states with a single nonzero Pauli modulus. We relate saturation to two-character sets and flat phase states, and classify a third-level phase-state family through five qubits.

We then test Jonah's strict law: does a sign carrier's spectrum on a hyperplane section determine its completion spectrum on the remaining observables? On a 71-point section of the real four-qubit quadric, two assignments give cospectral 16-by-16 carriers whose 64-by-64 completions have cubic traces 14976 and 15360 and distinct binary minima (<=344 < 347). A graph construction extends the gap to every N>=4 in case C3 (difference (3/2)8^(N-1)), and variants over R, C and H, a cone pair swap and a universal cubic-trace identity yield cospectral carriers with distinct completion spectra in all nine vertex cases for every N>=4, proving Jonah's Conjecture E. All nine cases, Corollaries 16 and 18, Lemmas 20 and 21 and the cubic-trace identity are proved in Lean 4 using standard axioms only, with exact verifiers and Tsotchke demonstrations. lean_scope: Lean 4.35.0 proves the spectral floor (Theorem 1), its quaternionic/Kramers refinement and elliptic quadrics (Theorem 2, Kramers.lean), the five-way saturation equivalences and (2^N-1)|S| = square (Theorems 3 and 4, SaturationTheory.lean), the exact degrees 75, 480 and 729344 with kernel-evaluated counts, the four-qubit C3 spectral certificate (42 declarations) and binary completion minima separation (Corollary 16, <=344 < 347, ConjectureEExtras.lean), case C3 for every N >= 4 (CarrierFamily.lean, 74 declarations), the general cone lift and case C11 (Corollary 18, ConjectureEExtras.lean), Lemmas 20 and 21, the universal cubic-trace identity (Theorem 22) and Table 8 character sums (ConjectureECore.lean, ConjectureECones.lean), and Theorem 19 across all nine vertex cases for every N >= 4 (plus N >= 3 for C1, C3, C6, C11; ConjectureE.lean; 49 audited declarations in VerifyNewFormalizations.lean, strictly within [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]). Remaining outside Lean: state-to-mask identifications of Table 1, Propositions 3, 4, 6 and 8-11, exhaustive enumerations of Theorems 12-13, printed C3 factorizations and relaxation gap 32, and Clifford orbit transport across hyperplane classes via Jonah [J3, Theorem B4].
